name: Heidi Ganahl
subject: The Mountain Minute: 4/30/2024
body:
Your daily rundown of REAL news for REAL Coloradans.
| | | | [](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.)
---
**PRESENTED BY[ROCKYMOUNTAINVOICE.COM](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.)**
| | Hi there,
This is the Mountain Minute for Tuesday, April 30, 2024.
- Heidi Ganahl
---
|
---
| | **TODAY'S TOP STORIES**
---
**['Citizens are not safe coming to the state capitol', Rep. Holtorf says on Stinchfield](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.) [](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.)** BY BRIAN PORTER, [ROCKY MOUNTAIN VOICE](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.)
[](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.)
Anyone choosing to visit the state's capitol is doing so at their own peril in Colorado, Minority House Whip Rep. Richard Holtorf [told Grant Stinchfield during a recent appearance on Real America's Voice.](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.)
"Denver citizens and Colorado citizens are not safe coming to the state capitol, or the capitol of Colorado," he said in a video clip posted on his Twitter/X account.
He's critical of City of Denver budget reductions, some to police in the state's capitol city, at the same time as out-of-control illegal migration, the clip details. He also details a concern toward crime related to illegal immigrants being unable to find work.
"When these immigrants can't find jobs, they're going to turn to crime," Holtorf said. **[READ MORE](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.)**
|
---
**[Colorado State University lands $25 million grant to boost methane detection work](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.) ** [COLORADO SPRINGS GAZETTE](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.)
* Colorado State University (CSU) has received a [$25 million grant from the U.S. Department of Energy](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.) to expand its Methane Emissions Technology Evaluation Center (METEC) in Fort Collins.
* METEC is the [largest and most active methane emissions detection test](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.) bed globally, aiming to enhance methane detection equipment.
* The facility, operational since 2017, covers eight acres and conducts over 200 days of testing annually on equipment for [detecting leaks in natural gas extraction](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.) and transmission systems.
* CSU's team at METEC operates more than [200 independently controlled leak points](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.) to simulate typical production system scenarios and conducts field research, including flying aircraft with methane detectors over gas production basins in Colorado.

**[READ MORE](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.)**
|
---
**[House Republican minority boasts passage of two bills into law, advancing five others they led](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.) [](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.)** [ROCKY MOUNTAIN VOICE](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.)
* [Two bills sponsored by Republican members](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.) of the Colorado House have been signed into law, along with several other bills enjoying Republican support, as the legislative session nears its end. Nine business days remain in the session, which concludes on May 8.
* [Senate Bill 87](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.), easing prescriptions of topical medications, sponsored by Rep. Mary Bradfield, and [House Bill 1072](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.), protecting victims of sexual crimes, sponsored by Rep. Lisa Frizell, have been signed into law.
* [Five other bills with Republican backing have passed](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.) the House, including [Senate Bill 125](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.), an interstate compact for child placement, sponsored by Rep. Gabe Evans, and [Senate Joint Resolution 17](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.) designating April 18 as Colorado Sportsmen's Day, sponsored by Rep. Mike Lynch.
* Additionally, [House Bill 1327](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.), a sunset review of physical therapy regulation, [House Bill 1371](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.) regulating massage facilities, and [House Bill 1431](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.) providing stable housing assistance for abuse survivors have passed through the House. [House Joint Resolution 1023](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.), opposing forced labor in electric vehicle manufacturing, sponsored by Rep. Ty Winter, has also advanced.

**[READ MORE](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.)**
|
---
**[George Soros is paying student radicals who are fueling nationwide explosion of Israel-hating protests](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.) ** [NEW YORK POST](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.)
* George Soros and associated groups are [financially backing anti-Israel protests on college campuses](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.) across the US, primarily through the Soros-funded Students for Justice in Palestine (SJP).
* USCPR, another Soros-funded organization, [pays individuals to organize campaigns supporting Palestinian causes](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.), with fellows earning up to $7,800 for community-based efforts and $2,880 to $3,660 for campus-based initiatives. Individuals paid by USCPR, like Nidaa Lafi, Craig Birckhead-Morton, and Malak Afaneh, have been instrumental in leading protests at universities such as the University of Texas, Yale, and Berkeley.
* Soros channels his contributions through a [network of nonprofits](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.) like Open Society Foundations and Tides Foundation, while former Wall Street banker Felice Gelman also provides financial support.

**[READ MORE](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.)**
|
---
**[Durango's hotel-to-housing project financing is a first in Colorado](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.) [](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.) ** [THE COLORADO SUN](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.)
* The Residences at Durango is [a pioneering project in Colorado](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.), converting a former hotel into 120 affordable housing units. This initiative aims to address the acute need for affordable housing in Durango, where high housing costs have been a significant challenge.
* Rents for the units will be affordable for those [earning between 30% and 60% of Durango's median household income](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.), targeting workers like teachers, restaurant staff, and retail workers.
* The project, [costing $35.6 million](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.), is financed through various means including tax credit financing, private activity bonds, and grants from state and federal sources.

**[READ MORE](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.)**
|
---
**ONLY ON ROCKY MOUNTAIN VOICE ⤵️**
**[Topping the 4th District special election ballot will be an Approval Voting Party candidate. But why?](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.)[](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.)** **BY BRIAN PORTER | STATE | APRIL 27** _Candidates from the two major parties appearing at the bottom of the 4th Congressional District 's special election ballot will have to hope voters read the whole ballot.___
**[Holtorf celebrates drawing second-line place on 4th District Republican primary ballot](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.)[](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.)** **BY BRIAN PORTER | STATE | APRIL 26** _District 63 State Rep. Richard Holtorf, R-Akron, will appear second on the Republican Party 's 4th Congressional District primary ballot, immediately following 3rd District U.S. Rep. Lauren Boebert, he announced Friday.___
**[Sloan: What to do about the Columbia University protestors](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.) ****[](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.)****BY KELLY SLOAN | COMMENTARY | APRIL 26** _What is it about Columbia University that seems to attract anarchic, fanatical madness? One may recall the 1968 campus revolt, which ultimately took the University well over a decade to recover from. Twenty years after that ignominy, a new generation of malcontents tried to replicate the whole thing, in the course protesting ... oh, who knows, Nicaragua, or Ronald Reagan or something._____

|

name: Karen Crnkovich
subject: The world is on fire
body:
So much has happened since you heard from me last.

The world is on fire, and we could be on the brink of a world war. Anti-semitism is reaching a boiling point on Ivy League campuses, yet we are stuck paying their student loans.

Kansans are still feeling and reeling from inflation and high-interest rates that have made daily life completely unaffordable. And our country’s leaders are failing to act.

At a time when our country and world need American leadership, our government is barely functional. It is completely unacceptable, and quite frankly, I’ve had enough... and I know you have too.

[That’s why I am running for Congress to represent YOU in Kansas’ third congressional district. But I need your help. ](https://secure.winred.com/karen-crnkovich-for-congress/donate)

As the owner of an HVAC and plumbing company, I know a thing or two about getting to the root of a problem, keeping systems running, and making things function again... all while maintaining my cool.

My company was just recognized as a Greater Kansas City Chamber of Commerce “Top 10 Small Business” for the second year in a row.

We have enough Do-Nothing people in Congress. What we need is someone who can get to work and fix the mess we’re in.

[I am the right person for the job. I just need your help to get there.](https://secure.winred.com/karen-crnkovich-for-congress/donate)

I have what it takes to fix the dysfunction in Congress and get our government functioning again. I’ve never been afraid of hard work and my business and community involvement speaks to that.

We are HOURS away from our next fundraising deadline, and all eyes are on us because the KC-03 seat is one of the big pick-up opportunities for Republicans.

But we need someone elected who can do the hard, tough, unglamorous work. I’m ready to roll up my sleeves, but I need to raise serious money to get my message far and wide.

[Make a difference by chipping in $500, $250, $150, $50, or $25 today to my campaign.](https://secure.winred.com/karen-crnkovich-for-congress/donate)

I sincerely thank you for your support. Together we can do this!

Karen

Karen Crnkovich for Congress, KS03 ____
[www.kcforkansas.com](http://www.kcforkansas.com/) ____
913-414-4446
#teamkc

Dear Peter,
In a world quick to label and divide, I stand before you not just as another candidate, but as a voice for authentic change.
Many wonder if I fit on the Right or the Left politically—some call me a conservative, others a liberal.
Let me be clear: _labels do not define my mission_.
You do!
I am a “classic liberal” in the sense that I believe in the values of JFK and my father RFK. Those were the days when Democrats championed free speech, peace, civil liberties, and (though it may surprise you) a strong border.
Before I unravel what all that means, I want to ask for your much needed contribution before the FEC filing deadline tomorrow night. body:
Which comes first, platform solutions or winning elections?

View this email in your browser (https://mailchi.mp/be0fec75ff4f/n41kepo7ku-12692970?e=25844e23a8)
https://ne.gop/?utm_source=Nebraska+Republican+Party&utm_campaign=d9317bc394-EMAIL_CAMPAIGN_1_2_2024_7_59_COPY_01&utm_medium=email&utm_term=0_72fdf24cb0-d9317bc394-21732365

** Good Morning Republicans,
------------------------------------------------------------
This weeks letter will be shorter then most... I think. :) It usually takes several hours on a Monday night to collect my thoughts and work through the theme of each newsletter. Sometimes I feel like I have so much to communicate, whether just updates on party business/procedures or attempting to give context or perspective on where we've come as a State Party. Sometimes I am challenged to articulate the frustration and disbelief I have that comes from becoming intuitively aware of peoples true motives in this political world. I get many emails that indicate an appreciation of the TRUTH. Which, I truly believe isn't so much about something I've necessarily revealed...this TRUTH...it's more of confirming what people have felt about politics and seen OF people IN politics for a long time. I get some emails that my newsletters are too divisive or harsh in tone, that we should all just get along for the sake of getting along.
This is where my email from last week originated when I phrased the simple question... "What do you want?" This question has so many nuances to it and can be said with different emphasis. "What do YOU want?" or "WHAT do you want?"
It's a question that conveys a problem in need of a solution and requires both parties to see a level of importance to the urgency of a decision.
Then sometimes, I have to take a step back and try to communicate a bigger picture. We all saw the big picture this week as unprecedented storms with destructive tornadoes effected a large geographically area for most of Eastern Nebraska. The big picture is that Nebraskans can drop all division when life is on the line. We don't ask what political party you are affiliated with when trying to clean up neighbors loss of houses and property. We come together around a common bond of supporting someone in need and that's the human element to a community. We bring our time, talents, and treasures to lift up those who are hurting and foremost.
In essence...BIG PICTURE...Nebraskan's saw the many challenges ahead for those who lost their homes, who were in need of help, and the decision to have all hands on deck was immediate. What gave people hope and the willingness to help where they could was the stability and organization that came from leaders. Because of the preparedness of the local authorities and then the launch points for rallying people like the community churches, solutions turned into action.
Back to the political world...I believe...actually I know, that Nebraskans see the Big Picture when it comes to the immediate challenges we face as a State.
✅We have to fix Nebraska's broken property tax system
✅We have to grow our economy through job creation and education of work identities
✅We have to strengthen and maintain the amazing rural communities and modernize the infrastructures
✅We have to support our agricultural system, the lifeblood of Nebraska's economy
✅We have to restore educational basics, safety of classrooms, and the excellence of Nebraska values, so our kids take ownership of the Nebraska Good Life and stay IN Nebraska.
✅We have to prioritize election honesty that uses common sense and transparency of voting - Election Accountability and Voter Verification.
✅We have to bring respect to Law and Order and address the rising mental health concerns that can easily start in supporting healthy families.
Folks, our challenges are not new and they are not unattainable. But they will require everyone in our party to see the Big Picture and work towards it together day-by-day. This WILL mean being held accountable as well as finding humility. This WILL mean that the change of culture is not just wishful thinking...change of mindset is a NECESSITY. Because...if the last 20 years of the Republican political environment was both inherently proactive and out of necessity sometimes reactive...then the solutions...would already be accomplished. We can't continue operating from the same political lens and expect success. We can't fear the new methodology that says "We will campaign or legislate based on our principles and not bend to the agendas of today!" We HAVE strong values that resonate with most Nebraskans.
Be an Unapologetic Constitutional & Platform Republican!
DONATE (https://ne.gop/donate/?utm_source=Nebraska+Republican+Party&utm_campaign=d9317bc394-EMAIL_CAMPAIGN_1_2_2024_7_59_COPY_01&utm_medium=email&utm_term=0_72fdf24cb0-d9317bc394-21732365) to the NEGOP. DONATE to your local GOP.
We will put your dollars to work connecting to more Republican voters state-wide.
We will put your dollars to work defeating Democrats at the local level.

Our State Convention is May 18th (https://ne.gop/convention2024/?utm_source=Nebraska+Republican+Party&utm_campaign=d9317bc394-EMAIL_CAMPAIGN_1_2_2024_7_59_COPY_01&utm_medium=email&utm_term=0_72fdf24cb0-d9317bc394-21732365) and we have an awesome Featured Speaker - Lt. General Michael Flynn! We will be showing his movie "Flynn - Deliver the Truth. Whatever the Cost." on Friday night, May 17th including a Q&A session

FLYNN Movie Premiere Tour
Friday, May 17^th Lincoln, NE
5:00pm Doors open

When the Arizona Supreme Court decided to enforce one of the most extreme bans on abortion in the country earlier this month, we saw a huge swing of support.
#

I’m at a bit of a loss, Peter.
When the Arizona Supreme Court decided to enforce one of the most extreme bans on abortion in the country earlier this month, we saw a huge swing of support.
People from coast-to-coast chipped in to help us fight back against Kari Lake and the MAGA extremists who are trying to take over our state.
In a really difficult moment, it was an incredible show of solidarity.
But over the last week or two, that support has fallen off. Things have slowed down quite a bit, and the timing is really terrible. This slowdown is happening as Kari Lake is criss-crossing the country at high-dollar fundraisers.
She is raking in cash, and she’ll use every dollar of it to beat us and impose her radical agenda.
Sorry to be so blunt here, but if we’re going to win in Arizona we can’t have bad days or slowdowns. We have to be at our best every single day between now and the election.
I know times are tough, I know there is a lot going on in the world, and I know there are a lot of campaigns asking you to donate. It can be really overwhelming. I get it.
And I never thought I’d need to ask so many people like you, people I might never meet, to support me and help defend our majority in the Senate. But today, to turn this around, that’s exactly what I have to do. I have to ask for your help.

A few years ago, members of the world’s elite met at the annual World Economic Forum in Davos, Switzerland, and launched the Great Reset initiative.

What is their plan, and what does it mean for America?

In short, they aim to transform the world economy. As Klaus Schwab--the founder and executive director of the Forum--wrote, “We need a ‘Great Reset’ of capitalism.” If successful, their plan would also have the effect of destroying our American way of life.

This initiative is not merely about economic reform. It is an attempt to impose global rule by so-called experts.

Some social media companies are censoring our efforts to promote a seminar we hosted on the Hillsdale campus that explored the topic of the Great Reset. Fortunately, we can communicate directly with you.

In this seminar, we...

* Consider the idea of the Great Reset and its implications for America.
* Explore how the ideology of “woke capitalism” is infiltrating large corporations.
* Delve into pro-freedom alternatives to this tyrannical plan.

Peter -- In its decision to overturn _Roe v. Wade_ , the Supreme Court majority wrote, “Women are not without electoral or political power.” No kidding. Those bragging about overturning _Roe_ have no clue about the power of women, but they found out when it was on the ballot in 2022. And 2023. It’s our job to make sure they find out again this year. **Whether or not we succeed is up to you, Peter. subject: Will you support my friends at GIFFORDS PAC?

Hi there, Jimmy Kimmel here. I know you’re used to seeing me on your TV screen, but today I’m reaching out to you about an important topic close to my heart: ending America’s gun violence crisis.
Gun violence isn’t always in the headlines, and it can be far too easy for us to go about our daily lives and forget that it’s happening each and every day. But for the families who now have empty seats at their dinner table—like the families who lost a child in Newtown, Parkland, or Uvalde—they can never, ever forget.
[**GIFFORDS is doing lifesaving work at the forefront of the gun safety movement, and I'm proud to be an ambassador for this incredible organization. Will you join me today in supporting GIFFORDS PAC by making a contribution to support their crucial work?**](https://go.giffords.org/go/14457?c0=giffords-em-apr24.Y_Rik7&refcode=em240430-1-30&t=2&akid=8024%2E3935704%2ElAcVwM)
**[DONATE](https://go.giffords.org/go/14457?c0=giffords-em-apr24.Y_Rik7&refcode=em240430-1-30&t=3&akid=8024%2E3935704%2ElAcVwM)**
Gun violence is a uniquely American epidemic. This year alone, we’ve experienced record numbers of mass shootings. The leading cause of death for children in our nation is gun violence.
This is the only developed country in the world where this happens. We have to do something to change this.
Laws such as universal background checks, safe storage laws, and extreme risk protection orders would help ensure that guns can’t fall into the hands of people who shouldn’t have access to them. We call these laws commonsense because that’s just what they are—common sense.
It is long past time for our representatives to do their job and truly represent the American people. The majority of Americans support commonsense gun safety legislation. Yet far too many of our politicians make the choice to stall the passage of lifesaving legislation because they’re afraid to stand up to the gun lobby.
[**This is not a moment where we can sit back. We must be loud and use our collective voice to make a change. So please, will you make a commitment to ending our nation’s gun violence crisis by donating $3 to my friends at GIFFORDS PAC today? The federal taxpayers, the American taxpayers who fund the government, are sick and tired of out-of-control spending - INCLUDING sending billions overseas to Ukraine.

|
---
Kevin Hern here.

**I recently voted against sending another $60 billion to Ukraine.**

_And, I would do it again in a heartbeat._

The federal taxpayers, the American taxpayers who fund the government, are sick and tired of out-of-control spending - INCLUDING sending billions overseas to Ukraine while our own Southern border is wide open.

I’ve long promised never to vote for more Ukraine funding without strong border security provisions to protect America. The U.S. has already sent billions in aid to Ukraine; we’ve done our part, but enough’s enough.

Further, we have no business sending tens of billions of dollars to Ukraine while doing absolutely nothing to end the crisis on our own Southern border.

I was one of the first Members of Congress to take this stand against further Ukraine funding without border security, and there isn’t anything that will make me change my beliefs on this.

The American people deserve better than this.

subject: I won’t ever forget it
body:
Kari Lake thinks the January Sixers are patriots. I think that anyone who supports those terrorists and traitors shouldn’t be allowed anywhere near the U.S. Senate.
| | | | |
---
| | |
---
| | |
---
| |

| You're getting this message because you’ve supported good causes and Democratic candidates. We need your support to continue fighting for our democracy. We love having you in our network, but if you no longer wish to hear from us, you can[ unsubscribe here](https://default.salsalabs.org/T28389d5e-46ea-4205-8a75-b54b496f1691/368d17ff-e836-4168-8049-c5f0900fbbf9) _._

|

| | | | | I won’t ever forget it, Peter. Standing on the House floor. Hearing shouts, pounding, breaking glass. Barricading the door, teaching my colleagues how to use their gas masks. Texting my staff, telling them to hide. I carried a rifle in Iraq and all I had to defend myself on January 6th was a pen. But I was ready to fight. And after that day, Trump’s loyalists crawled right back to him. Witnessing them reject what they lived through, watching them ignore the testimony of the police officers that defended us that day while they were beaten, bloodied, pepper sprayed, cursed at... it makes me sick. Kari Lake thinks the January Sixers are patriots who were “invited in” — she even campaigns with them. I think anyone who supports those terrorists and traitors shouldn’t be allowed anywhere near the U.S. Senate. This race in Arizona is just me and her. It’s on us to stop her march to more power and influence. Whoever wins in Arizona is going to determine which party holds the Senate, and could even decide whether Trump takes back the White House. I need you with me, and I need you to take this race seriously. [**Please split a donation of $20 — that or anything you can give — between my campaign and Blue Amp Action to crush Kari Lake’s campaign and defend our democracy.**](https://default.salsalabs.org/T00035e90-f5bd-4a38-b975-c75a232f395c/368d17ff-e836-4168-8049-c5f0900fbbf9)

body:
#

Hey everybody, it’s Mark.
I’ve spent a lot of time over the last year traveling the country to support friends in tough races. Wherever I go, people ask me what it’s going to take to hold the Senate this year.
It’s a good question. Our margin is extremely thin, and we’re on defense in nearly every competitive race.

That’s why I’m writing to you today. We’re doing a ton of work to support pro-democracy candidates around the country, whether it’s supporting their campaigns or building infrastructure. body:
And why I hope you’ll join our people-powered movement.
# [](https://act.hillharper.com/go/421?t=1&akid=1207%2E62735%2EzwtZJC)
Peter,
In a minute I’ll share why I put my acting career aside to run for the U.S. Senate, but first: **My campaign has a critical end-of-month deadline tonight, and _every dollar_ is critical to our success. [Will you rush any amount, no matter how small, to hit our goal before midnight?](https://act.hillharper.com/go/1417?t=2&akid=1207%2E62735%2EzwtZJC)**
I've worn many hats throughout my life, from lawyer to union organizer, actor to author, and cancer survivor to single father. I’m a small business owner, too — I have a coffee shop right here in Detroit. **But above all, I'm a servant leader driven by a passion for making life better for everyone around me.**
Growing up in the Midwest with two doctors as parents, I learned early on the value of public service. It's a lesson that has stayed with me throughout my life, from my days at Harvard Law School to my time on the set of The Good Doctor. I've always believed that true leadership means putting the needs of the people above personal ambition, and I’ve committed myself to building a career that reflects those values.
That’s why I've written books to connect with and empower young people, and established a foundation to help them achieve their goals.
It’s why I joined the UAW and SAG-AFTRA strikes last year to support their fight for better pay and working conditions.
**And of course, it’s why I put my acting career aside to run for the U.S. Senate.**
You see, I believe that the challenges facing our nation demand new, dynamic leadership — not the same bought-and-paid-for politicians who let us down year after year. We need responsive leaders who will put public service over personal gain, fight for our most urgent priorities, and embody the authentic representation that every Michigander deserves.
_But I can't do it alone._ And since I’m not taking a cent of corporate PAC money, I need your help to build a grassroots movement that puts the power back in the hands of the people.
**[So, with our end-of-month fundraising deadline coming up at midnight, I need to ask for your support today. Please, chip in any amount to fuel our people-powered campaign in the weeks ahead.](https://act.hillharper.com/go/1417?t=3&akid=1207%2E62735%2EzwtZJC)**

In 2008, a roadside bomb in Afghanistan left me with burns over half my body. This was my vehicle after the explosion.

[](https://links.greatamericatoday.com/u/click?_t=e3c9a4cac7f248a39c2a3d920479a441&_m=e998b0c9b0fd4e20b634a26f8a24eb1c&_e=DyWvfMRrFZujciwtOKc7LVtTo5cYtXiaUqNdY6bpJ-yaZ2MWErdkZUPHxKn33O0M2NPxvVVgqoNmbrSn_u5Q796iTlyqraoJBLUjwEB_CCao4EFLCBMfYw9rRmD4JtdsyGB9T9JhTrdWPG872PmbMCvzEgwXtDa-IG3pYDHBTmCXTdTzdOHBD_3RoANtYlehgliHpE4sxUNMNG3vuZ9AeG2x-GiXnHXMb3T79k3x-JUx0e_7-ppbX3VwPzdC5AOcQGjV04PeREMXhFLVVdTrRg3yTbbLlmr1U06EGHcyXlY9079b5NJOlA0UdRPFiiX-741gXxzbYrsVGq2TbPbsWu_CWeMJbS7ItfJfgLzdn89caGpIVCIxRhnBJsL2zl2F5CBGo6gD1vUuPitJjO_4_Gs4y2v8Iaz0o3JHBXBlwGie_N3leWryr6kI159nzDFT)

My path to recovery wasn't easy -- I spent months wondering if my life could ever be the same, asking myself why God spared me that day. **[But that was God's way of speaking to me, THIS was His message to me...His plan for me.](https://links.greatamericatoday.com/u/click?_t=e3c9a4cac7f248a39c2a3d920479a441&_m=e998b0c9b0fd4e20b634a26f8a24eb1c&_e=DyWvfMRrFZujciwtOKc7LVtTo5cYtXiaUqNdY6bpJ-yaZ2MWErdkZUPHxKn33O0M2NPxvVVgqoNmbrSn_u5Q796iTlyqraoJBLUjwEB_CCao4EFLCBMfYw9rRmD4JtdsyGB9T9JhTrdWPG872PmbMCvzEgwXtDa-IG3pYDHBTmCXTdTzdOHBD_3RoANtYlehgliHpE4sxUNMNG3vuZ9AeG2x-GiXnHXMb3T79k3x-JUx0e_7-ppbX3VwPzdC5AOcQGjV04PeREMXhFLVVdTrRrOBtQIw4azJoYGJtynP6cUurdAd6RAc-dZbv6ZVzbKm8lEVb6wU6qxLTNLz3_qMiZHfhFKaAK_JA6JHuYaBTT13rIjdcdyCABYHkeK-wDWj2lui0iGZpwcxdvzl38NaaVreXitkSYeCjxCljJug63q-uMLUOIWAnfGG-vp2_NVn)** Friend, I realized that my life would NEVER be the same, but that was okay. I was alive for one reason: **_[My new life belonged not to me, but to Him. ](https://links.greatamericatoday.com/u/click?_t=e3c9a4cac7f248a39c2a3d920479a441&_m=e998b0c9b0fd4e20b634a26f8a24eb1c&_e=DyWvfMRrFZujciwtOKc7LVtTo5cYtXiaUqNdY6bpJ-yaZ2MWErdkZUPHxKn33O0M2NPxvVVgqoNmbrSn_u5Q796iTlyqraoJBLUjwEB_CCao4EFLCBMfYw9rRmD4JtdsyGB9T9JhTrdWPG872PmbMCvzEgwXtDa-IG3pYDHBTmCXTdTzdOHBD_3RoANtYlehgliHpE4sxUNMNG3vuZ9AeG2x-GiXnHXMb3T79k3x-JUx0e_7-ppbX3VwPzdC5AOcQGjV04PeREMXhFLVVdTrRnkerMN3Ok-fKrXxBFLAwT0EchTRdlsQ983MHyeOqN1CrDWkQ43RJg6q6fZiZLFhOQcZ-X9bAlseIxEjWUfiH5YRZqqVF701RCj0hNxgL_-KMS9MjrgnndV7SHf1Zb8HGc5mg8U8grfi8sHPfFOecfFVz7ECHvCapNcMAb05TNGB)_** [**_That 's why I've lived every day since with three things in mind: My country, my family, and God Himself. _** ](https://links.greatamericatoday.com/u/click?_t=e3c9a4cac7f248a39c2a3d920479a441&_m=e998b0c9b0fd4e20b634a26f8a24eb1c&_e=DyWvfMRrFZujciwtOKc7LVtTo5cYtXiaUqNdY6bpJ-yaZ2MWErdkZUPHxKn33O0M2NPxvVVgqoNmbrSn_u5Q796iTlyqraoJBLUjwEB_CCao4EFLCBMfYw9rRmD4JtdsyGB9T9JhTrdWPG872PmbMCvzEgwXtDa-IG3pYDHBTmCXTdTzdOHBD_3RoANtYlehgliHpE4sxUNMNG3vuZ9AeG2x-GiXnHXMb3T79k3x-JUx0e_7-ppbX3VwPzdC5AOcQGjV04PeREMXhFLVVdTrRlVIYz4BybNTzu275OOp5rOgAICBdwXN45-bwrQHMq15LeHKboBEY5c9_EnN5NqskciUCrF8qn-MJdz0O7Pv-lGi2TdbW9orahzaapSlAsrVHgtKMqrhCR8Iz75S6H4gbrTZ8qHn0WuUh5IKppQwcVCX7DZfuiPIHMHSJx1WbnKN) God used the tragedy that resulted in my injuries to tell me something. Through 3 years of recovery and over 30 surgeries - I was never alone. Not for one second. God stayed with me through it all and he made it clear to me that I was NOT called to wish for my old life. **[Instead, I was called to live my new life to the fullest in service to Him.](https://links.greatamericatoday.com/u/click?_t=e3c9a4cac7f248a39c2a3d920479a441&_m=e998b0c9b0fd4e20b634a26f8a24eb1c&_e=DyWvfMRrFZujciwtOKc7LVtTo5cYtXiaUqNdY6bpJ-yaZ2MWErdkZUPHxKn33O0M2NPxvVVgqoNmbrSn_u5Q796iTlyqraoJBLUjwEB_CCao4EFLCBMfYw9rRmD4JtdsyGB9T9JhTrdWPG872PmbMCvzEgwXtDa-IG3pYDHBTmCXTdTzdOHBD_3RoANtYlehgliHpE4sxUNMNG3vuZ9AeG2x-GiXnHXMb3T79k3x-JUx0e_7-ppbX3VwPzdC5AOcQGjV04PeREMXhFLVVdTrRq1Fdk3_GvCVwDObIisb_vgzDWzdGco4njE4mtTVczfIbr1-MyORHUeyi4VJ9cbgaIxg6n0szdtu4Nc_QRESO3TvLrYDN3sVuNlXGyt8cidIb8Y3mkHpmlFz-8Yg3KAqDEHqx-v_rAwS7rQuyVR4simZyGlMdjDucQItdZpDzUdK)** That's why I spent the last 15 years starting my family, serving fellow veterans through the business I started, and most recently, _**[and launched my campaign to become the next U.S. Senator from Nevada.](https://links.greatamericatoday.com/u/click?_t=e3c9a4cac7f248a39c2a3d920479a441&_m=e998b0c9b0fd4e20b634a26f8a24eb1c&_e=DyWvfMRrFZujciwtOKc7LVtTo5cYtXiaUqNdY6bpJ-yaZ2MWErdkZUPHxKn33O0M2NPxvVVgqoNmbrSn_u5Q796iTlyqraoJBLUjwEB_CCao4EFLCBMfYw9rRmD4JtdsyGB9T9JhTrdWPG872PmbMCvzEgwXtDa-IG3pYDHBTmCXTdTzdOHBD_3RoANtYlehgliHpE4sxUNMNG3vuZ9AeG2x-GiXnHXMb3T79k3x-JUx0e_7-ppbX3VwPzdC5AOcQGjV04PeREMXhFLVVdTrRsF0aOk-W3U6Ny6WR4rjGt1NDRS3Xr84lfhdO4nQDp5x5KpVqinAuhD0W29N_TIans52fKtMLOH0MeIwMiykayLNKnU7jCyH8-8wjl1anEGs4yvsMNgpB1QkoTPtjo90IO03CdE1YPkrGRSgd7rDODeylE-U1itc1FpiGSJJFfUh)**_ America is at a tipping point. Corrupt leaders are leading us into total madness. Our border is collapsing. Parents are being cut-off from their children in schools. We're spending away their future and the future of our children's children. I'm running for U.S. Senate to bring a new generation of Conservative leadership to Washington D.C. name: The Office of Delegate Briana D. Sewell
subject: Del. Sewell's April 30th Newsletter
disclaimer_text: Paid for by Friends of Briana Sewell
body:
[https://prod.cdn.everyaction.com/images/van/NGP/NGP13/1/87444/images/New%20Sewell%20Delegate%20Logo%20.png]
April 30th Newsletter
Dear neighbors,
I hope all is well with you and yours. I’ve returned from Richmond after our April 17th reconvened session. Each year reconvene is set for six weeks after the end of the regular legislative session so that the General Assembly can review the governor’s actions on all legislation sent to his desk.
Reconvene and Special Session for the Budget
The General Assembly can override vetoes or amendments with a 2/3rds vote, or can accept amendments and return them to the governor for his signature. During this year’s reconvene, 32 House Bills (HBs) and 22 Senate Bills (SBs) were returned back to the Governor in their enrolled form, meaning the amendments suggested by the governor were rejected. Additionally, the General Assembly sent one bill back that was agreed to in-part. The Governor has up to 30 days from April 17th to either sign or veto these 55 measures.
Finally, in the late afternoon on April 17th, both the House and Senate passed HJ 428 "Applying to the Governor to call a special session and establishing a schedule for the conduct of business coming before such special session.” In accordance with Article IV, Section 6 and Article V, Section 5 of the Constitution of Virginia, the Governor called the General Assembly into a special session via a proclamation. This special session is part of the Governor and General Assembly’s joint agreement to return to budget negotiations and produce a final compromise before the July 1st budget deadline.
Issue of the Week: K-12 Education (Part 2)
As discussed in last week’s newsletter, in an effort to continue to share information about legislation passed during the General Assembly, below is part two of all K-12 education bills which passed during the 2024 legislative session. If you have any questions about these bills, I encourage you to reach out to my office and we will be glad to share additional context.
Teachers & Licensure
The process to become licensed to teach can be confusing, expensive, and time-consuming in a time when it is more important than ever to recruit and retain high quality teachers. Several bills this year dealt with teacher licensure and compensation. HB187 [https://lis.virginia.gov/cgi-bin/legp604.exe?ses=241&typ=bil&val=hb187] required that the General Assembly fund teacher salaries at or above the national average for the next three biennium. Other bills work to change and remove unnecessary barriers to teacher licensure. HB632 [https://lis.virginia.gov/cgi-bin/legp604.exe?ses=241&typ=bil&val=hb632] and SB352 [https://lis.virginia.gov/cgi-bin/legp604.exe?ses=241&typ=bil&val=sb352] make it easier for teachers from out of state to transfer their licenses to Virginia, HB269 [https://lis.virginia.gov/cgi-bin/legp604.exe?ses=241&typ=bil&val=hb269] makes it easier for career switchers to enter the teaching profession through a special career switcher license, and SB142 [https://lis.virginia.gov/cgi-bin/legp604.exe?ses=241&typ=bil&val=sb142] gives flexibility to superintendents to offer short term licenses to fill urgent vacancies. Proudly, my bill HB 731 [https://lis.virginia.gov/cgi-bin/legp604.exe?ses=241&typ=bil&val=sb142] , which works to remove an unnecessary, outdated, and duplicative teacher licensure exam was signed by the governor.
Curriculum & Graduation Requirements
A large number of bills heard by the K-12 education committee during the 2024 legislative session had to do with what students are learning in classrooms and what critical knowledge all students should have before they graduate and enter the working world. Many of these bills dealt with teaching students about sensitive and important real world issues such as risks of opioid use ( HB134 [https://lis.virginia.gov/cgi-bin/legp604.exe?ses=241&typ=bil&val=hb134] ), sexual harassment prevention ( HB215 [https://lis.virginia.gov/cgi-bin/legp604.exe?ses=241&typ=bil&val=HB215] ), mental health ( HB603 [https://lis.virginia.gov/cgi-bin/legp604.exe?ses=241&typ=bil&val=HB603] and HB224 [https://lis.virginia.gov/cgi-bin/legp604.exe?ses=241&typ=bil&val=hb224] , governor’s amendments rejected), menstrual health ( HB1221 [https://lis.virginia.gov/cgi-bin/legp604.exe?ses=241&typ=bil&val=HB1221] ), allergy awareness and reaction prevention ( HB121 [https://lis.virginia.gov/cgi-bin/legp604.exe?ses=241&typ=bil&val=HB121] ), and climate change and environmental literacy ( HB1088 [https://lis.virginia.gov/cgi-bin/legp604.exe?ses=241&typ=bil&val=HB1088] , vetoed by the governor). Other bills dealt with foundational graduation and academic questions such as literacy instruction ( HB647 [https://lis.virginia.gov/cgi-bin/legp604.exe?ses=241&typ=bil&val=hb647] ) and ensuring students have the ability to fulfill certain elective requirements through obtaining certain workforce credentials ( HB1345 [https://lis.virginia.gov/cgi-bin/legp604.exe?ses=241&typ=bil&val=hb1345] ). All but two (HB224 and HB1088) of the bills listed above were signed into law by the governor and will become requirements for students beginning after July 1st, 2024. Students will see changes to their curricular experience beginning in the 2024-2025 school year.
School Boards
School boards govern the day-to-day budgetary, administrative, and policy questions of schools and many of the bills in this year's K12 education subcommittee provide guidance or direct the department of education to create model policies for how school boards should deal with these issues. Two bills focused on how school boards should include youth voice in their work, both through public comment at school board meetings ( HB253 [https://lis.virginia.gov/cgi-bin/legp604.exe?ses=241&typ=bil&val=hb253] ) and adding a student representative to their board ( HB958 [https://lis.virginia.gov/cgi-bin/legp604.exe?ses=241&typ=bil&val=hb958] ).
Many pieces of legislation dealt with school board record keeping, disclosure, and administrative policies, including bills regarding the sharing of information with school leaders about justice-system-involved youth ( HB1317 [https://lis.virginia.gov/cgi-bin/legp604.exe?ses=241&typ=bil&val=hb1317] ), providing timely employment verification ( HB355 [https://lis.virginia.gov/cgi-bin/legp604.exe?ses=241&typ=bil&val=hb355] ), and sharing parental notifications for sexually explicit content in instructional material ( HB571 [https://lis.virginia.gov/cgi-bin/legp604.exe?ses=241&typ=bil&val=hb571] - vetoed by the governor).
Other bills clarify current law or govern use of public funds by school boards, including clarifying that school construction funds can be used for technical education programs ( HB462 [https://lis.virginia.gov/cgi-bin/legp604.exe?ses=241&typ=bil&val=hb462] ), ensuring that students in foster or kinship care are able to stay enrolled in their current public school tuition free through the end of the school year after a change in their guardianship or placement ( HB777 [https://lis.virginia.gov/cgi-bin/legp604.exe?ses=241&typ=bil&val=hb777] ), and allowing schools to partner with telehealth providers for mental health services ( HB919 [https://lis.virginia.gov/cgi-bin/legp604.exe?ses=241&typ=bil&val=hb919] ).
Testing & Compliance
Last but not least, several bills this session dealt with compliance, testing, and Department of Education administrative issues that are critical to assessing school quality, administering legislatively authorized programs and funding, and administering the regulatory side of public education. These bills include administrative legislation to establish an office of community schools within VDOE ( SB608 [https://lis.virginia.gov/cgi-bin/legp604.exe?ses=241&typ=bil&val=sb608] ), to require the VDOE to notify school boards of federal legal obligation to participate in JROTC ( HB1231 [https://lis.virginia.gov/cgi-bin/legp604.exe?ses=241&typ=bil&val=hb1231] ), to require VDOE and VDH to streamline school health entrance forms ( HB1279 [https://lis.virginia.gov/cgi-bin/legp604.exe?ses=241&typ=bil&val=hb1279] ), and to establish a farm to school program task force ( SB314 [https://lis.virginia.gov/cgi-bin/legp604.exe?ses=241&typ=bil&val=sb314] ).
Other bills focused on improving the collection of educational data and creating policies around state testing, specifically, providing alternative growth assessment mechanisms to state testing ( SB435 [https://lis.virginia.gov/cgi-bin/legp604.exe?ses=241&typ=bil&val=sb435] ), codifying policies which allow access to expedited test retakes for students ( HB1451 [https://lis.virginia.gov/cgi-bin/legp604.exe?ses=241&typ=bil&val=hb1451] ) and creating a work group to review the current capabilities and future needs of the Virginia Longitudinal Data System and the Virginia Workforce Data Trust ( HB1083 [https://lis.virginia.gov/cgi-bin/legp604.exe?ses=241&typ=bil&val=hb1083] ).

But the budget battle playing out between Gov. Glenn Youngkin and the Democratic-led General Assembly is anything but routine.

Virginia set to receive $156 million from U.S. Environmental Protection Agency program. President Joe Biden stopped by Prince William Forest Park in Triangle on Monday, as the country celebrated Earth Day, to tout two initiatives to combat climate change: expanding solar access and creating jobs to fuel America’s environmental efforts.
*I was proud to join President Biden and several other local and state and federal elected officials for this exciting announcement.

Gov. Glenn Youngkin and lawmakers have agreed to work together on the biennium budget, after clashing for weeks over two distinctly different spending plans. A special session will be held on May 13, Youngkin and lawmakers in both chambers announced Wednesday, to consider the revamped budget and prevent a shutdown ahead of July 1, when the current budget expires.

The link in the text message is created to impersonate a toll facility’s or collection service’s name, and phone numbers appear to change between states. Each year reconvene is set for six weeks after the end of the regular legislative session so that the General Assembly can review the governor’s actions on all legislation sent to his desk. Reconvene and Special Session for the Budget The General Assembly can override vetoes or amendments with a 2/3rds vote, or can accept amendments and return them to the governor for his signature. During this year’s reconvene, 32 House Bills (HBs) and 22 Senate Bills (SBs) were returned back to the Governor in their enrolled form, meaning the amendments suggested by the governor were rejected. Additionally, the General Assembly sent one bill back that was agreed to in-part. The Governor has up to 30 days from April 17th to either sign or veto these 55 measures. Finally, in the late afternoon on April 17th, both the House and Senate passed HJ 428 "Applying to the Governor to call a special session and establishing a schedule for the conduct of business coming before such special session.” In accordance with Article IV, Section 6 and Article V, Section 5 of the Constitution of Virginia, the Governor called the General Assembly into a special session via a proclamation. This special session is part of the Governor and General Assembly’s joint agreement to return to budget negotiations and produce a final compromise before the July 1st budget deadline. If you have any questions about these bills, I encourage you to reach out to my office and we will be glad to share additional context. Teachers & Licensure The process to become licensed to teach can be confusing, expensive, and time-consuming in a time when it is more important than ever to recruit and retain high quality teachers. Several bills this year dealt with teacher licensure and compensation. HB187 [] required that the General Assembly fund teacher salaries at or above the national average for the next three biennium. Other bills work to change and remove unnecessary barriers to teacher licensure. Proudly, my bill HB 731 [] , which works to remove an unnecessary, outdated, and duplicative teacher licensure exam was signed by the governor. Curriculum & Graduation Requirements A large number of bills heard by the K-12 education committee during the 2024 legislative session had to do with what students are learning in classrooms and what critical knowledge all students should have before they graduate and enter the working world. Many of these bills dealt with teaching students about sensitive and important real world issues such as risks of opioid use ( HB134 [] ), sexual harassment prevention ( HB215 [] ), mental health ( HB603 [] and HB224 [] , governor’s amendments rejected), menstrual health ( HB1221 [] ), allergy awareness and reaction prevention ( HB121 [] ), and climate change and environmental literacy ( HB1088 [] , vetoed by the governor). Friend,
Our islands deserve a member of Congress focused on the Virgin Islands, not scoring cheap stateside political points.

We can end Stacey Plaskett's political career by getting Ronald Pickard on the ballot as the Republican candidate for Congress in 2024.

Remember when Plaskett said President Trump needs to be shot? That's the kind of disgraceful behavior that does nothing to help the Virgin Islands.

"There is no such thing as Democratic or Republican problems. Just people problems." — Ronald Pickard
Ronald is circulating petitions to qualify ahead of the mid-May filing deadline. He needs to collect the signatures of at least 25 registered Republican voters from each district.

On St. Croix, stop by the Pickard Building in downtown Christiansted or call/text Ronald at 340-626-2362 to arrange a meetup.

In the St. Thomas-St. John district, Ronald will be over for carnival Thursday and the Republican boot camp this Friday at The Westin, Frenchman's Reef.

Please join me in signing Ronald's petition.

Thanks,
Valerie Stiles

body:
Now that we’ve officially kicked off the general election campaign, Ted Cruz is calling in every favor he's got.

| **This is amazing: TWO polls in a row show Colin Allred TIED with Ted Cruz!**

_**But here's the bad news:**_ Now that we’ve officially kicked off the general election campaign, Ted Cruz is calling in every favor he's got. GOP mega donors have already poured more than $51 MILLION into his campaign, and as you read this, they're flooding him with even more to try to defeat Colin.

# FROM THE DESK OF ALAN DERSHOWITZ
---
| | Dear Peter, In over sixty years in the legal profession, I've experienced first hand the impact of both good journalism and bad journalism — mostly the latter — and just how important and rare it is to get things right.

**In today's media landscape there are far too many publications that get things wrong.** Many are more concerned with the political implications of a story than the basic facts.

**The New York Sun is different.** It's a paper that places principle over politics and people over party.

Its in-depth coverage of the legal challenges faced by President Trump serve as a case in point.

When I defended President Trump during his first impeachment, I faced an avalanche of criticism, but few papers made sufficient effort to fully appreciate the significance of the legal arguments.

The Sun's deeply knowledgeable leadership, including its editor Seth Lipsky and associate editor A.R. Hoffman are themselves students of the Constitution. It shows in their coverage, which I find to be first rate.

It will be no secret to you that I don't agree with everything that can be found in the Sun's pages, but I can say with confidence that its re-emergence is among the most important recent developments in American journalism.

I've been impressed by the Sun's growth so far, but I know it faces an uphill battle, one that I have pledged to join.

**The Sun's success will be a gift to the American people and to the cause of truth.** But to succeed, we need you to join us. I highly encourage you to join the Sun today.

Every person matters in this effort.

Don't wait. The battle to restore American journalism starts now.

body:
Unintended Consequences | | | | [View this email in your browser](https://mailchi.mp/c188225c9c27/conforti-for-congress-8400463?e=25f4fa3311)
---
| | |
---
| | | Dear Peter,

The protest encampments sweeping college campuses of elite universities is unsettling for a number of reasons. Our First Amendment Right to assemble and protest is engrained in the identity of who we are as a nation. But where do you draw the line?

When protests become combative or destroy property - can one still fall back on their First Amendment Right as a means of avoiding arrest and prosecution? Who is protecting those outside the protest?

The lack of universities' decisive action when the protesters are fighting law enforcement and breaking into buildings will have long-term repercussions. By not drawing a line in the sand, the university has already begun to feel the effects through loss of donors and employers not hiring their graduates. The reputations of these universities will be tainted, and enrollments may drop. In 1970, several students died in a war protest on the campus of Kent State University in Ohio. While the circumstances were different, the end result is that many colleges and universities closed, according to the Kent State University website.

Photo Credit: New York Times

We all have the Right to protest - no question. However, no one has the Right to destroy property or endanger others.

By supporting failed democrat policies, Sean Casten is perpetuating the lack of boundaries that is leading to the chaos we are seeing across our great nation. When I am in Congress, I will work to bring common sense back to the forefront and protect the constituents District 6, and all Americans.

You can help. Please consider making a donation to the campaign. Your contribution will go a long way in helping us win! Click the link below to make a donation today.

[](https://conforti4congress.us6.list-manage.com/track/click?u=7fd34b7284bf7f5e87a4e45e5&id=1e8e85f0f3&e=25f4fa3311)

Your support is greatly appreciated.
---
| Thank you,

Niki Conforti
Candidate
Illinois 6th Congressional District

| [](https://click.historyoftheday.com/u/click?_t=930f96a60371422687dbefcfca24c32b&_m=51357f150a194e18a4cb16520746f03f&_e=4ZYNXDfcnDraoHtnaTpYF0z1FXASxYON8EJelxjOEZ7WhH7ABBvylzX7cx37Lqpp2LT9Doc39SipzIBqxKbMjhw8imggDAnDlW-7GsVyUkgSstdLaF8xqq8csSaahbfAJt1bbLKKdbQ-JxLUvpMMxouArCWbYlVdx0yWFQxCHatJKfckN64wvlNO7DC5IxqiDMWKqTf_RWSIFrwZsWWT3pZVySSK2--6dwI-be9kY-6xuk9z7mbxCxYUGrlg9G3W1b5aRwXiMtj-iJL7qScYnuYe9cXyr_xKqz4zUqhZxPGxvFVqKRfpCABC4u7FaMZlSXOGSK2mEBSj1Lelria7vVXdgq2kC2hhBNYbqzGJHFNBa-sfrcq0rzwZnvY6dhrG8ZGvAEVIX7CeKMvRnGKJDg%3D%3D)

Fellow American,

I made a promise when you hired me as State Treasurer four years ago. As the next U.S. Representative for West Virginia’s 2nd Congressional District (God willing), I’m ready to do it again.

I promised you that I would get to work for all West Virginians and deliver on our shared goals; goals that will take our state from good to great, and make it the best place for people to live, work, and raise their families.

As I run for a new office, I promise to continue pushing West Virginia to be the best it can be. I’m prepared to fight for you by working to:

* Decrease inflation and put hard-earned dollars back into the pockets of Americans

* Invest in our teachers and children so the next generation can reach their full potential (no more CRT curriculum in schools)

* Put our economy back on track & get folks back to work

* Secure our border to STOP the drugs, crime, and human trafficking poisoning our communities

* Support law enforcement and our military, who work to keep us safe at home and overseas

| [**STAND WITH RILEY MOORE**](https://click.historyoftheday.com/u/click?_t=930f96a60371422687dbefcfca24c32b&_m=51357f150a194e18a4cb16520746f03f&_e=4ZYNXDfcnDraoHtnaTpYF0z1FXASxYON8EJelxjOEZ7WhH7ABBvylzX7cx37Lqpp2LT9Doc39SipzIBqxKbMjhw8imggDAnDlW-7GsVyUkgSstdLaF8xqq8csSaahbfAJt1bbLKKdbQ-JxLUvpMMxouArCWbYlVdx0yWFQxCHatJKfckN64wvlNO7DC5Ixqia656FtEtbmJTCq1BCiI42DGjl3MQxNG2ZuaJyVSogs3Q6usRKdoM8uWX9C3JZ4ilpKZTzuB8kFqO6o3tyKOJK5u02GeXHalLaxGdgrL-6i7eXfIL98asbChV74B6FTWhclCXG-l_UnzFCG_uimXQugHxjaSu2Ycbseu2vq99DzP9tDHv-9F2yclE6Ytc7jnnVzw2AbLbdiaTnuM7zXgdXg%3D%3D)
---

We can do all of this together, not because of partisan views, but because we know these common sense solutions will deliver the best results for all of West Virginia and America.

All of these shared goals are at risk from the far Left Democrats who are trying to take control of the House, Senate, and White House in 2024. They are trying to lead West Virginia and America down a path toward higher taxes, higher crime, higher inflation, unsafe communities, and fewer jobs.

As your next Congressman, I refuse to let that happen. I’m not going to stand by and let them steal your paychecks and raise your taxes to fund their bogus plans. I’m not going to let our border remain wide open and crime flood into our communities. I’m not going to let them take jobs out of West Virginia.

I promise to find common-sense solutions to defend West Virginia and prevent the Left from tearing apart the American Dream even further. I appreciate your support as I aim to deliver on these promises.

[**STAND WITH RILEY MOORE**](https://click.historyoftheday.com/u/click?_t=930f96a60371422687dbefcfca24c32b&_m=51357f150a194e18a4cb16520746f03f&_e=4ZYNXDfcnDraoHtnaTpYF0z1FXASxYON8EJelxjOEZ7WhH7ABBvylzX7cx37Lqpp2LT9Doc39SipzIBqxKbMjhw8imggDAnDlW-7GsVyUkgSstdLaF8xqq8csSaahbfAJt1bbLKKdbQ-JxLUvpMMxouArCWbYlVdx0yWFQxCHatJKfckN64wvlNO7DC5Ixqia656FtEtbmJTCq1BCiI42DGjl3MQxNG2ZuaJyVSogs1m6cdm61zTkYO4WTwGW-AWoBl2M1epKL9OkxtArH9FSemcctthrCBG37iJBMaXyH_iYgqBOZoL2SXMJqcMqmPuMs8E3xPeZ69CFFOiRvQmE3D0574bavSjJhRfbfO6knKFXC_7BuRFeWOx27k5xn-874GlxANLfStgQGxyIg_UfQ%3D%3D)

Riley Moore

clean_body: When you hired me as State Treasurer in 2020, I made a promise - now I’m ready to do it again as your next U.S. Representative for West Virginia Congressional District 2. | Fellow American, I made a promise when you hired me as State Treasurer four years ago. As the next U.S. Representative for West Virginia’s 2nd Congressional District (God willing), I’m ready to do it again. I promised you that I would get to work for all West Virginians and deliver on our shared goals; goals that will take our state from good to great, and make it the best place for people to live, work, and raise their families. As I run for a new office, I promise to continue pushing West Virginia to be the best it can be. I’m prepared to fight for you by working to: Decrease inflation and put hard-earned dollars back into the pockets of Americans Invest in our teachers and children so the next generation can reach their full potential (no more CRT curriculum in schools) Put our economy back on track & get folks back to work Secure our border to STOP the drugs, crime, and human trafficking poisoning our communities Support law enforcement and our military, who work to keep us safe at home and overseas | We can do all of this together, not because of partisan views, but because we know these common sense solutions will deliver the best results for all of West Virginia and America. All of these shared goals are at risk from the far Left Democrats who are trying to take control of the House, Senate, and White House in 2024. They are trying to lead West Virginia and America down a path toward higher taxes, higher crime, higher inflation, unsafe communities, and fewer jobs. As your next Congressman, I refuse to let that happen. I’m not going to stand by and let them steal your paychecks and raise your taxes to fund their bogus plans. I’m not going to let our border remain wide open and crime flood into our communities. I’m not going to let them take jobs out of West Virginia. I promise to find common-sense solutions to defend West Virginia and prevent the Left from tearing apart the American Dream even further. I appreciate your support as I aim to deliver on these promises. Thank you for your support, Riley Moore | RILEY MOORE: CONSERVATIVE FOR CONGRESS. Washington is all tied up in putting politics over principle. It’s time to put a stop to it and start putting PRINCIPLES OVER POLITICS - starting with YOU! | Paid for by Moore for West Virginia. Hi Peter,

An alarming report on the current state of maternal care in Louisiana was just published, and we wanted to fill you in.

The article states that in the aftermath of the state’s abortion ban, pregnant women have been given “risky, unnecessary surgeries, denied swift treatment for miscarriages and ectopic pregnancies, and forced to wait until their life is at risk before getting an abortion.”

They found that doctors were using “extreme caution,” leading to unnecessary deaths in pregnant women. This is because, under the new law, **doctors would face penalties of up to 15 years in prison and $200,000 in fines for performing an abortion.**

Here’s what women in Louisiana are going through:

❌ **Denying care to seriously ill patients until their lives are “irrefutably” at risk:** Doctors are delaying lifesaving treatments to avoid breaking the law, even in cases in which the pregnancy is not viable and is deadly to the mother. “One patient with an ectopic pregnancy said her care was delayed so long that her fallopian tubes ruptured.”

❌ **Unnecessary C-sections:** The report found that when a patient’s water broke _before the fetus was viable_ , they would receive unnecessary C-sections to empty their uterus instead of receiving a sometimes medically _necessary_ abortion procedure or medication. As detailed in the article, when compared to an abortion under these circumstances, C-sections carry “far greater risks for increased hemorrhaging, compromised future fertility, and other complications.”

Modern medicine has found ways to ensure women do not need to endure this. We are failing these women.

❌ **Delaying prenatal care into the second trimester:** OB-GYNs are delaying routine prenatal care until at least 12 weeks of pregnancy. This delay can be dangerous for women who may have complications, such as blood clots or an undiagnosed ectopic pregnancy. “Without treatment, some pregnancy-related problems can lead to birth defects, stroke, heart attack, or even death.”

**Here’s the thing:** People's lives are at severe risk because of the Louisiana abortion ban, and this is especially true for Black and low-income women. According to NPR, Louisiana has some of the HIGHEST rates of maternal mortality and morbidity in the nation, and Black women are 2X as likely to die compared to white women.

From New York City to Los Angeles, Americans of conscience have embraced remarkable demonstrations of solidarity over the past week, only to encounter equally remarkable examples of state violence and repression.
For better or worse, the past week has offered plenty of reasons for outrage at Washington, as well as opportunities to celebrate--and support, extend, and amplify--resistance to it.
_What happened to the Occupy Movement in 2011 set the stage for the suppression of speech and dissent sweeping the country today._
I wrote this post to help readers better understand and recognize fascism in America, and also to help highlight important examples of grassroots dissent.
### **2024: Occupy Education**
The ongoing Israeli genocide in Gaza has not only exposed the [lawlessness](https://substack.com/redirect/a16148e8-bced-4fb0-8640-b40a5c342b04?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) of Washington's bipartisan empire, its disturbing willingness to [invite civilian casualties](https://substack.com/redirect/8e1e0351-721d-43b3-90dc-15ced0821fae?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg), and the priority it places on the interests of [corporate weapons manufacturers](https://substack.com/redirect/77450382-6bae-4de5-8bf0-20c37be3037b?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg), but also the solidarity shown by activists from all walks of life who remain undeterred and [committed](https://substack.com/redirect/aa6649ff-9c08-4a86-8d21-b406ea382446?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) to basic human rights principles that our nation once fought a World War to establish.
It has also brought America's hypocrisy to the fore, by exposing not only how U.S. weapons sales have enabled genocide, but also how little anyone in government supports free speech, dissent, or democracy.
_Help inform your friends!_
[ Share](https://substack.com/app-link/post?publication_id=1018597&post_id=144172655&utm_source=substack&utm_medium=email&utm_content=share&utm_campaign=email-share&action=share&triggerShare=true&isFreemail=true&r=1hvr60&token=eyJ1c2VyX2lkIjo5MDUwMTE5MiwicG9zdF9pZCI6MTQ0MTcyNjU1LCJpYXQiOjE3MTQ0OTIxOTAsImV4cCI6MTcxNzA4NDE5MCwiaXNzIjoicHViLTEwMTg1OTciLCJzdWIiOiJwb3N0LXJlYWN0aW9uIn0.9OWAPTU6PLEyKi68eZ1UhcQ1oXPfePVAH_Y81J4tMOs)
[Columbia University in New York City](https://substack.com/redirect/15cef2af-32e9-4806-aa08-d6545ebf7171?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) has emerged as one flashpoint, particularly because school administrators berated by Republican members of Congress in a [recent congressional hearing](https://substack.com/redirect/1b7535f0-8348-4510-912e-749ec40ed435?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) responded to their pressure by imposing authoritarian measures to suppress student speech--and ultimately, cancel in-person classes for the rest of the academic year. When Republican House Speaker Mike Johnson visited Columbia recently, throngs of irate students protested his speech, while Governor Kathy Hochul [described](https://substack.com/redirect/3735aa2e-497f-4307-a7fc-cded9aa09453?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) Johnson as "politicizing" campus tension and "adding to the division" that continues to escalate.
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/adfbd709-0742-49f4-a136-a35b814d0f17?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
Students who learned enough from their education to take action on the principles that they learned about in class have been disciplined--and even suspended from the university--prompting students at dozens of other campuses across the country to organize protests, marches, and occupations in their respective areas across the country.
Many of those campuses have experienced tumult and tension as a result. Last Thursday, over [100 students were arrested](https://substack.com/redirect/df6839dd-2418-4981-a283-6e945b8fb4af?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) at Emerson College in Boston, while nearly 100 were detained at the University of Southern California and 34 more (plus a reporter) were arrested at the University of Texas in Austin. Earlier in the week, [nearly 150 students, faculty, and others were arrested](https://substack.com/redirect/df6839dd-2418-4981-a283-6e945b8fb4af?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) on the campus of New York University, while a "Free Palestine Camp" at the University of California-Berkley in which hundreds of students have joined has [stretched into its sceond week](https://substack.com/redirect/92da34ad-8ece-4c4e-ba7b-07ec8e68d570?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg). At UCLA, thousands of students participated in a series of protests despite the intimidation of militarized police and [violence by vigilantes](https://substack.com/redirect/27677351-6004-4af4-9101-841451ffa11d?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) seemingly [encouraged](https://substack.com/redirect/8d75b054-3afa-4627-b5b3-68a01fb75abe?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) by Sen. Tom Cotton (R-AR).
### **Forcing Biden 's hand**
Some of the controversies have impacted President Biden directly and prompted responses from the White House.
For example, knowing that [Biden's re-election prospects have dimmed](https://substack.com/redirect/0d4b261f-26bb-4b17-81e8-0d7cc65e157b?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) due to his foolish support for Netanyahu's genocide in Gaza, and recalling his [reliance on Black voters](https://substack.com/redirect/be1e2729-2ad7-43df-a6b8-b02c77a78718?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) whose interests Washington has relentlessly undermined for decades, the Biden campaign recently [planned](https://substack.com/redirect/6680358c-c959-42a3-8c77-6dfe3d024abe?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) for President Biden to deliver the May 19 commencement address at Morehouse College. Morehouse is a historically Black university in Atlanta with a storied legacy. Its alumni include Dr. Martin Luther King, Jr.
Morehouse Provost Kendrick Brown [said](https://substack.com/redirect/4f74d59b-90fb-4625-b75e-d43dd8615db7?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg), "From our perspective, really having a sitting president come to Morehouse offers an incredible opportunity. This is something that is in line with Morehouse's mission and also with this objective of being a place that allows for engagement of social justice issues and moral concerns."
Rather than encounter the fawning reception that he expected, however, Biden's visit has already drawn protests week in advance.
Political science professor Andrew Douglas [said](https://substack.com/redirect/4f74d59b-90fb-4625-b75e-d43dd8615db7?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg), "I've spoken with several faculty members who say under no conditions are they going to sit on a stage with Joe Biden." He went on to say that "I have not had a conversation with a student who's happy about this," and that "[Morehouse's] priority should be...to try and ensure that under no circumstances are the police brought to bear on our students," since Morehouse "students do not have the same privileges that Ivy League students typically do, and confrontations with the police can turn deadly for our students."
Douglas added that "We have a legacy of being at the forefront of justice movements," which requires speaking truth to power, rather than trying to curry favor with it.
[Across Atlanta](https://substack.com/redirect/778a1d4b-5336-47e7-9258-2e84679ecd6c?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg), students who organized a peaceful encampment at Emory University released a statement explaining that their stance against domestic police militarization "is interconnected with global movements against oppressive state practices, most notably the Palestinian struggle for liberation." Police retaliated by subjecting them to chemical weapons, gun violence, and [dozens of arrests](https://substack.com/redirect/26885d12-4139-4f43-b335-f0f7157f1a59?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg).
The chair of the university's philosophy department was among the figures arrested in what another professor (who was also arrested) described as "[a war zone](https://substack.com/redirect/35f11654-dd8c-444c-bf6d-427de287209f?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)."
One student activist at Emory [echoed](https://substack.com/redirect/0afe57fa-03e7-4220-a580-ffecf18be656?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) the concerns of faculty at nearby Morehouse, saying:
> "I'm a senior at Emory University. Today we were trying to build an encampment ... We were out here chanting peacefully ... All of a sudden a huge patrol of police ... basically swarmed the entire crowd.
> Students of color were significantly targeted throughout the process. There were Black students that were being tased, there were Black students that were being teargassed. I got teargassed as I was trying to leave the protest."
It's worth noting that [tear gas has long been banned as an instrument of war](https://substack.com/redirect/8cbc40e5-748e-4dec-8943-2247f431b085?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg).

[Upgrade to paid](https://substack..kuIATJ6GC3CH8Rjpz-27SNyfaG8NZUWunkeY2YHOms4?&utm_medium=email&utm_source=subscribe-widget-preamble&utm_content=144172655)
What does it suggest about the United States that authorities here use it so widely against civilians exercising rights guaranteed under the Constitution?
### **2011: Occupy America **
13 years ago, the world celebrated the [Arab spring](https://substack.com/redirect/e0aaf219-01d1-41a2-9fdb-2352d75d2cdb?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg). Across north Africa and the Middle East, activists from Tunisia to Egypt and beyond came together across social classes and professions to challenge autocracy and corruption. Risking and enduring severe brutality in some cases, they reminded the world [what democracy actually looks like](https://substack.com/redirect/171485b3-9059-4d07-8a64-615b1c3b340d?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg).
While many Americans paid attention to the events, most tragically misinterpreted them. Rather than take inspiration from the social mobilization confronting corruption, American observers generally took the [self-serving approach](https://substack.com/redirect/b05ad2b7-56a1-4aec-ba0e-7e16266d1ded?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) of giving credit to Facebook and Twitter. Many focused on tech platforms used by vulnerable activists to help connect with each other--and eventually, topple their governments--rather than the movement for democracy itself.
Ironically, those platforms went on to [implement unilateral changes](https://substack.com/redirect/86382f76-7579-4431-bee5-5c38b05733f7?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) that vastly diminished their utility as social organizing tools, in the service of making them more valuable levers for promoting commercial goods and services. That ultimately represents yet another case of capitalism undermining democracy, which I wish were a less consistent theme in the United States.
In any case, some of us did pay attention to the Arab spring and learn the lessons that it offered.
That fall, hundreds of thousands of us around the country [occupied public spaces](https://substack.com/redirect/c5093865-f89d-484f-8ceb-c432da925aea?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) in an effort to not only reclaim them for our communities, but also discover common cause, learn from each other, and challenge an establishment that remains [so ignorant, a full decade later](https://substack.com/redirect/4f31bc49-2324-4d42-8b81-8db7c952572c?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg), that it repeats its errors without any meaningful reflection.
The Occupy Movement was [viciously suppressed](https://substack.com/redirect/c9c499af-80c4-40ae-b089-e29217b3a130?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) through a [combination](https://substack.com/redirect/3e098c77-864a-496b-94d2-e52d9a436179?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) of state violence, surveillance, persecution, and prosecution. It was largely [coordinated by federal authorities](https://substack.com/redirect/e3875df2-b368-41b5-b670-ccc5a81d4bb1?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) during an era when Washington was led by a Democratic president, at the same time that a supposedly liberal press consistently downplayed the movement's concerns, covered up police violence, and mischaracterized participants as self-indulgent, rather than outraged to the point of being willing to risk state violence.
What happened to the Occupy Movement in 2011 set the stage for the suppression of speech and dissent sweeping the country today.

It offers an indication of_**why** _authorities have seemed hellbent on suppressing speech, rather than supporting the constitutional rights to which they swear oaths of allegiance..._

**Press Contact** : Damon Drew
damon@emiliasykesforcongress.com

| **Emilia Sykes Earns Endorsement of Ohio AFL-CIO By Unanimous Vote** **President Burga: Endorsement “a Testament to Her Dedication to Improving the Lives of Working People...”**
---
| AKRON, OH — Today, Emilia Sykes for Congress announces that the Ohio AFL-CIO endorsed the re-election of Congresswoman Emilia Sykes by a unanimous vote of the Executive Board.

"The unanimous decision of the Ohio AFL-CIO Executive Board to endorse Congresswoman Emilia Sykes’ re-election is a testament to her dedication to improving the lives of working people in her district," **said Ohio AFL-CIO President Tim Burga.** "In the past two years Congresswoman Sykes has delivered America's largest investment in infrastructure, capped insulin prices for seniors, secured meaningful federal investments to ensure the 13th District continues to lead the way in polymer innovation and stood on the picket line with union members in their fight for a fair contract. Emilia fights for us in Congress and stands with us at home and we proudly continue our support for her."

"Since her time in the Ohio Statehouse, Emilia Sykes has been a staunch advocate for working families in the greater Akron region. Representative Sykes has earned organized labor’s endorsement and broad support and we will work tirelessly on her re-election bid," **said David Prentice, Executive Secretary of the Tri-County Regional Labor Council.** "Due in large part to Emilia’s policy work and leadership in Congress, Summit County is seeing positive growth for the middle-class and we need to keep this momentum going."

"Representing the people of Stark County and the 13th District, Congresswoman Emilia Sykes has stood up and delivered for working people and trade unions," **said Joe Sterling, President of the Hall of Fame Labor Council.** "Representative Sykes is not only delivering unprecedented economic development opportunities for our communities, but she is also ensuring labor's voice is at the table in applying the millions of dollars of federal investment to benefit everyone in Stark County."

“I’m proud to have earned the endorsement of Ohio’s biggest pro-worker organization who fights everyday to ensure our workers are treated fairly and given the respect they deserve,” **said Emilia Sykes.**
“In Congress, I have fought for higher wages, safer working conditions, and better benefits for workers and I am excited to have the support of the Ohio AFL-CIO in that fight.”

Sykes is serving the second year of her first two-year term representing Ohio’s 13th Congressional District. Her top priority is making government work for her district. During her tenure, she has brought back more than $100 million in federal dollars to to improve public transportation and infrastructure in Northeast Ohio, including $500,000 for the North Canton Arrowhead Water Well Project, $959,752 for the New Franklin Water and Sewer Project, and $1 million for the Lake Anna Revitalization Project.

Friend, my motto has always been that when you love this country, you fight for the people who make it work. That's what I'm doing every day in the Senate.
I'm fighting for the Dignity of Work . No matter where you're from or what kind of work you do, hard work should pay off for everyone. Whether you punch a clock or swipe a badge, earn a salary or make tips, are raising children or caring for an aging parent, I'll fight for you.
I'm fighting for accountability. For years, we've seen corporations lobby for tax breaks and bad trade deals that hurt workers. I'm not afraid to stand up to Wall Street or take on Big Pharma to level the playing field.
I'm fighting for our fundamental rights. My opponent has made it clear he doesn’t have our best interests at heart. I will always fight for a more equal and inclusive country.
But here's the deal, friend: I need you to fight with me. I'm facing my toughest race yet, and polls show me neck and neck with my Trump-backed opponent. He’s spending millions of dollars to flip this seat and the Senate red, and I can't fight back without your help.
I need to raise $50,000 by midnight tonight to fight back, and I'm counting on your grassroots support to get there. Please, will you split a $20 donation between my campaign and Serve America to help me win in Ohio, defend our Democratic Senate majority, and keep fighting for you in the Senate?
